title: How do we draw a regular hexagon with each side four centimetres?
description: A circle of radius four centimetres, the same radius stepped round it from a point, and the six points joined. Each step makes an equilateral triangle with the centre, so the sixth step comes back to the start. Keeko's raised hand shows the same six sided cells in a beehive.
teaching_notes: One idea: the side of the hexagon is the radius of its circle, and six sixty degree angles fill the turn. Watch for students who change the compass opening between the circle and the steps.

source: Construct a regular hexagon with side 4 cm using a ruler and
video_script.why: The child builds a hexagon to an exact size from six equilateral triangles.
video_script.substitution: Each step round the circle makes one equilateral triangle with the centre.
video_script.anchor: A circle of radius four centimetres with centre O, drawn with a ruler and a compass.
video_script.payoff_line: Each side is four centimetres and each angle is one hundred and twenty degrees.

final_answer.value: ABCDEF, with six sides of 4 cm and six angles of 120°
final_answer.spoken: a hexagon with six sides of four centimetres and six angles of one hundred and twenty degrees

maths_rules: Compass set to 4 cm with the ruler; circle with centre O; A on the circle.
OA = OB = AB = 4 cm, so triangle OAB is equilateral and angle AOB = 60°.
Five more cuts of 4 cm give C, D, E, F; each triangle at O is equilateral with angle 60°.
6 x 60° = 360°, so the next step from F lands back on A.
Each side is 4 cm; each corner angle is 60° + 60° = 120°.
video_script.design: One circle, one compass opening, six equilateral triangles round O. Real life closes with a beehive face of hexagonal cells, drawn.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We want a six sided shape with all sides equal and all angles equal. Each side must be four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We have only a ruler and a compass.
How can we draw it?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A six sided shape with equal sides and equal angles is called a regular hexagon.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A triangle with three equal sides is called equilateral, and each of its angles is sixty degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, each side is four centimetres, and we have a ruler and a compass.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to construct the regular hexagon.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, open the compass to four centimetres against the ruler.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Draw a circle with centre O, and mark a point eigh on it.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, with centre eigh and radius four centimetres, cut the circle at B.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Triangle O eigh B has three sides of four centimetres. It is equilateral, and angle eigh O B is sixty degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: with the same opening, cut C from B, D from C, E from D, F from E. 6 × 60° = 360°, so the next step lands back on A

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, keep the same opening and cut C from B, then D, E and F.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six angles of sixty degrees make three hundred and sixty degrees, a full turn.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The next step from F lands back on eigh.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: join A, B, C, D, E, F in order. Every side = 4 cm. Each corner angle = 60° + 60°

marks.m1: the six points are joined in order
marks.m2: two triangles at one corner are shaded and their angles added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, join eigh, B, C, D, E and F in order. Every side is four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>At each corner two triangles meet, so each angle is sixty plus sixty.

beats.on_screen: Answer: ABCDEF, six sides of 4 cm, six angles of 120°

marks.m2: the sides and the angles are labelled and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The hexagon eigh B C D E F has six equal sides and six equal angles.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each side is four centimetres and each angle is one hundred and twenty degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This shape is found in a beehive. The front face is made of hexagonal cells.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Bees keep eggs safe and store food in these cells.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The cells fit together with no gaps, so no space is wasted.
